Version: URL segment v-1-18-x and page version selector 'v1.18.x' match target v1.18.0. Content: the atomicity sentence is present verbatim in the versioned OpenAPI schema description backing this page — ChangeAliasesOperation in docs/redoc/v1.18.x/openapi.json:11093 'Alias changes are atomic, meaning that no collection modifications can happen between alias operations.' — which is generated from the in-repo docstring lib/storage/src/content_manager/collection_meta_ops.rs:346-348; nuance: the page's rendered summary prose as fetched shows only 'Updates aliases for the specified collections.', the atomicity sentence lives in the request-body schema description; also note the doc's own wording defines atomicity via the no-interleaving clause, while the contract assertion additionally elaborates 'no intermediate state is observable'. Endpoint: registry entry aliases+update = POST /collections/aliases, actions required array, timeout optional >=1, 200 result:boolean — all matched by the exercised requests and the observed 200 {"result":true} positive.

http_semantics.note: The invalid action was correctly surfaced as HTTP 404 with error body; this candidate is NOT an error-masking case. The violation is state residue after the 404: actions preceding the failing action remain durably committed.

contract_grounding.assertion_text_quoted: alias operations in one request are applied atomically - no intermediate state is observable and no collection modification can interleave
contract_grounding.note: The observed batch (mixed#1: [create al3 valid, create on no_such_col]) was rejected with 404 yet al3 remained committed, and mixed#3's valid delete leaked through a rejected batch — operations in one request were demonstrably NOT applied atomically, which is inside the quoted assertion's own domain (one-request alias batch), so violates=true. Interpretation nuance for the auditor: the OpenAPI sentence's 'meaning that' clause frames atomicity as no-interleaving-between-operations; the contract's description quotes that spec wording and the assertion extends it to all-or-nothing observability; the source function's own comment also claims 'performs several alias changes in an atomic fashion'.

source_grounding.call_chain_traced: POST /collections/aliases -> src/actix/api/collections_api.rs:180 update_aliases handler -> dispatcher.submit_collection_meta_op(CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases) [lib/storage/src/dispatcher.rs; the ChangeAliases arm at :168 only decides node-sync, no pre-validation] -> TableOfContent::perform_collection_meta_op [lib/storage/src/content_manager/toc/collection_meta_ops.rs:82-85] -> update_aliases [:298-338] -> per-action validate_collection_exists/collections_ops.rs:25 (source of the observed 404 'Collection `X` doesn't exist!') interleaved with AliasPersistence::insert/remove [alias_mapping.rs:66/72, each saving data.json via atomic_save_json immediately]. No pre-validation pass over the whole batch, no rollback on mid-batch failure: the '?' early-return leaves prior actions durably applied — exactly the observed order-dependent partial commit (valid-then-invalid leaves residue; invalid-first leaves none). gRPC face converges: src/tonic/api/collections_api.rs:124 -> conversions.rs:285-297 -> same CollectionMetaOperations::ChangeAliases. Versioned OpenAPI prose is generated from lib/storage/src/content_manager/collection_meta_ops.rs:346-348 docstring via src/schema_generator.rs.
source_grounding.outcome_detail: validation_absent refers specifically to the all-or-nothing transactional application the contract requires: no two-phase validate-then-apply and no rollback exist in the source; per-action validation IS present (it fired, producing the 404). by_design_in_source NOT granted: the only atomicity-related comments ('performs several alias changes in an atomic fashion'; 'Lock all collections ... Prevent search on partially switched collections') describe lock-based isolation and even claim atomicity — none declares partial-commit-on-failure intended; lib/storage/tests/integration/alias_tests.rs covers happy-path batches only (all .unwrap()), with no failure-path atomicity test. All grep hits on update_aliases/ChangeAliases were pursued (handler, dispatcher, toc, conversions, tests, schema_generator).

mundane_explanation.surviving: interpretation risk on the word 'atomic': the spec sentence's own 'meaning that' clause ('no collection modifications can happen between alias operations') reads as an isolation/no-interleaving guarantee, and the source implements exactly lock-based isolation (locks are held across the whole loop); under that narrow reading the durable partial state after a rejected batch is under-specified by the doc sentence rather than literally contradicting it — but no explicit maintainer statement declares partial-commit-on-failure intended, and the function comment's own claim ('performs several alias changes in an atomic fashion') is contradicted by the observed durable residue. Adjudication of this reading belongs to the chain-auditor.
